rationale.org-governance: Enterprise framework assigns reviews, records, testing, accountability, and standardized processes.
rationale.automation-bias: Time-pressed developers trust compiling, superficially tested migrations despite semantic errors.
rationale.oversight-scaling-inversion: Migration volume overwhelms reviewers, making high-risk inspection cursory rather than thorough.
rationale.oversight-theater: Review persists nominally but lacks time and institutional mandate for depth.
rationale.rules-based-checks: Differential testing deterministically compares original and converted systems across representative inputs.
rationale.risk-routing: Output discrepancies independently trigger targeted human review of divergent cases.
rationale.hitl-workflow: Defined scoping, component-validation, and certification checkpoints give engineers blocking authority.
rationale.oversight-explanation: Provenance records expose generation context and modifications for human understanding.
rationale.regulatory-compliance: Framework addresses SOX, MiFID II, auditability, and regulated-system verification duties.
rationale.provenance-auditability: Persistent records trace source, model, run, edits, and approving engineer.
rationale.framework: Three-part review, provenance, and differential-testing design is reusable in enterprise pipelines.
rationale.design-only: Mechanism is specified but neither implemented nor empirically evaluated.
rationale.agentic: LLMs migrate whole modules and codebases delivered at gate granularity.
rationale.steering: Pre-migration scoping determines which modules the AI converts.
rationale.risk-quality: Functional-equivalence failures and reliability receive focal analysis and testing mitigation.
rationale.risk-overreliance: Unwarranted developer trust receives focal analysis and checkpoint-based mitigation.
